root_cause: The exported MainActivity took a nested Intent from its EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT extra and started it as is, so any app could use Element's identity to open Element's non-exported activities; the fix starts the next intent only if it resolves to Element's own package and to one of five allowlisted activities.
notes: Affects Element Android 1.4.3 through 1.6.10; fixed in 1.6.12. The fix adds an Intent.isValid() check in MainActivity with an allowlist (HomeActivity, MainActivity, RoomDetailActivity, ThreadsActivity, LiveLocationMapViewActivity). Give the auditor vector/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml too, so the exported MainActivity is visible. CVE-2024-26132 (FileProvider scope) is a different root cause with a different commit and is not part of this sample.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: When uploading files that other apps shared in (ReceiveExternalFilesActivity to UriUploader to FileUploader), the app opened the received file URIs with its own permissions and blocked its private storage only with a raw startsWith("/data/data/") string check, so other locations of its private data (such as its app-specific media directory) passed and were read and uploaded; the fix rejects URIs that point into the app's private paths and returns ERROR_SENSITIVE_PATH.
notes: Fixed in Nextcloud Android 3.21.0. 1194a5c is the merge commit of PR #10544 (merged 2022-08-05), so the ^ ref is the first parent. The removed check in FileUploader.java was `if (file.getStoragePath().startsWith("/data/data/")) return`; the new UriUploader.kt (converted from Java) rejects private paths, and its tests cover /data/data/<package>/ and Android/media/<package>/. That other spellings of the private path also passed the old check is an inference from the fix, not stated in the advisory. The HackerOne report was not readable. PR #9645 was an earlier, unmerged attempt. Include app/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/files/services/FileUploader.java in the audit even though it is outside audit_scope.

Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The firefox://open-url deep link handler (RouteBuilder.makeRoute, .openUrl case) passed the url query value to a tab without checking its scheme, relying on the javascript: block in the WKWebView navigation delegate, which WebKit does not call on this load path, so another app could open a javascript: URL that ran in the current page's origin; the fix routes only http/https web pages.
notes: Fixed in Firefox for iOS 123. 379470e is the merge commit of PR #17827 (Bugfix FXIOS-7331, merged 2023-12-20). The existing javascript: block is in BrowserViewController+WebViewDelegates.swift (per the Bugzilla bug); the assignee noted the WebKit delegate methods are not called for this load. The same advisory also lists CVE-2024-26281 and CVE-2024-26282, which are separate bugs.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The iOS WKScriptMessageHandler (userContentController:didReceiveScriptMessage: in CDVWKInAppBrowser.m) took the id field of a message posted by the untrusted page shown in the InAppBrowser and passed it unchecked as the callbackId to the shared commandDelegate sendPluginResult:callbackId:, so the page could deliver forged results to any pending callback of any plugin in the host app; the Android implementation already validated the id, and the fix limits it to ^InAppBrowser[0-9]{1,10}$.
notes: Affects 3.1.0 through 6.0.0; fixed in 6.0.1. e0bd9dc is the commit of PR #1152 (fix(ios): check callbackId with regex, merged 2026-05-20). Keep both src/android and src/ios in scope: comparing the two platform handlers is one route to the bug. The Android-side regex check is stated in the PR description; I did not read the Android code.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The app PIN (passcode at start) was enforced only by the main app UI, while the File Provider extension that serves the same account files to the iOS Files app did not check whether a passcode was set, so turning on the Files app integration exposed the files without the PIN; the fix makes FileProviderExtension throw notAuthenticated when a start passcode is enabled.
notes: Fixed in Nextcloud iOS 4.7.0. GitHub shows only the short merge hash 64e9bef for PR #2344 (merged 2023-01-31); resolve the full hash in the repo. The fix adds a check using CCUtility.getPasscode() and CCUtility.isPasscodeAtStartEnabled() in FileProviderExtension.swift and a new File Provider Extension UI target that shows the error; which FileProviderExtension method got the check was not visible. The auditor also needs the passcode code in iOSClient to know the lock exists. Requires physical access to an unlocked device. The HackerOne report was not readable.

root_cause: The iOS plugin built SQLite statements with string formatting, including the file name taken from the download server's Content-Disposition header (UPDATE task SET file_name=...), so a server could rewrite task rows (URL, stored request headers, saved_dir) that are later replayed or used as the write destination; the fix binds parameters in DBManager and sanitizes file names.
notes: Affects flutter_downloader through 1.11.1 on iOS; fixed in 1.11.2 (changelog: Security update for iOS (#887)). 1d19dbb is the merge commit of PR #887 (merged 2023-09-11). A second cause in the advisory: the task database download_task.sql sat in the app's Documents directory, which host apps that set UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace expose to the Files app, so local users could edit it; PR #887's diff does not move the database (1.11.2 also lists #829, Support file store in any iOS directory). The researcher's article says the database was relocated; I could not confirm where.

root_cause: AuthActivity.onAuthenticationSucceeded() treated the callback itself as proof of authentication without a Keystore-backed CryptoObject, so hooking the callback bypassed the biometric check; the fix creates a biometric-bound AES key CryptoObject and validates the returned cipher before reporting success.
notes: No CVE assigned. Affects versions before 8.3.6; fixed in 8.3.6. Requires local instrumentation (for example a hooking framework on a rooted device). The fix commit title is Harden Android biometric auth; it adds createCryptoObject() and validateCryptoObject(). Only the Android side is covered by the advisory.

root_cause: The library's embedded-web-view AuthenticationAgentActivity was declared with [Activity(..., Exported=true)], which goes into every host app's manifest, so any local app could start the authentication activity with its own input (content injection into the web view, denial of authentication); the fix sets Exported=false.
notes: NuGet package Microsoft.Identity.Client. Two affected ranges: 4.48.0 to 4.59.0 (fixed in 4.59.1) and 4.60.0 to 4.60.2 (fixed in 4.60.3), so 4.60.0 shipped without the 4.59.1 fix. Commit 413e319 (Ashok's fix (#4714)) is the fix OSV lists; I did not check which release line it landed on. Only Android targets are affected.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The native delete()/set()/next() plugin methods, callable from the app's web layer, joined the caller's bundle id into a path under versions by string concatenation, without the containment helper the plugin already used for zip entries, and getBundleInfo() returned a harmless non-builtin record for unknown ids, so the guard protecting builtin and current bundles passed and recursive deletion could leave the bundle directory; the fix validates ids with resolveBundleDirectory() and fails closed.
notes: No CVE assigned; advisory published 2026-09-23. The advisory lists affected versions <= 8.47.3 and patched 8.51.23 (with 5.51.23, 6.51.23 and 7.51.23 on the LTS lines); the status of versions in between is not stated. e9a2fe6 is the merge commit of PR #920 (merged 2026-09-22). The same iOS logic lives in ios/Sources/CapacitorUpdaterPlugin; add it to the audit. PR #919 (manifest path traversal, GHSA-47wj-8cw3-4459) is a separate fix and not part of this sample.

root_cause: Markup saved an edited (cropped or redacted) screenshot back over the original file through ContentResolver.openFileDescriptor with mode w, which since Android 10 no longer truncates, so when the new image was shorter the tail of the original image stayed in the file and could be recovered; the correct mode is wt.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Pixel Update Bulletin March 2023, reference A-264261868, component Markup, information disclosure. The root cause comes from the researchers' public write-ups (the Android 10 change to ParcelFileDescriptor.parseMode), not from a patch. The same mistake pattern is independent of Pixel: any app that rewrites a file in place with a non-truncating mode.
